hed: DOJ asks Supreme Court to unblock expanded SAVE citizenship checks for voter rolls
dek: Solicitor General D. John Sauer on Tuesday asked the justices to stay U.S. District Judge Sparkle Sooknanan’s June order vacating DHS’s modified Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) system after a divided D.C. Circuit refused a stay. The overhaul added Social Security number lookups and bulk searches so states can seek citizenship confirmation for registered voters. Chief Justice John Roberts directed challengers to respond by 4 p.m. EDT Sept. 15 in DHS v. League of Women Voters (26A308). Older, individualized SAVE queries remain available while the expanded system stays blocked.

byline: Event summary from public filings and named outlets

cl.body: Democracy Docket, SCOTUSblog, and CBS News emphasize Judge Sooknanan’s finding that the modified SAVE system violated privacy and Social Security statutes, D.C. Circuit’s refusal to revive bulk citizenship checks, and challengers’ warnings that outdated Social Security flags can put eligible — including naturalized — voters at risk of wrongful purges.

cr.body: Washington Examiner, Law Commentary, and the Justice Department’s stay papers stress Sauer’s claim that Sooknanan’s order is “indefensible,” that SAVE only notifies states whether citizenship can be confirmed rather than removing voters itself, and that blocking Social Security–linked bulk checks before the midterms undercuts election integrity.

stack_blurb: Roberts: challenger replies due 4 p.m. EDT Sept. 15 (26A308).
seo_description: DOJ asked the Supreme Court to stay a ruling blocking DHS’s expanded SAVE citizenship database for state voter-roll checks; challenger replies due Sept. 15.
